_purpose: Machine-independent scientific catalogue of validated Bulk Silicate Moon (BSM) reference compositions. This file is the tracked, canonical source of BSM entries and is safe to load in tests and in a clean clone. It intentionally does NOT contain a perplex_dir or build_template_file: those are runtime-infrastructure fields and belong in a local configs/models.json (which is git-ignored). To generate compositions or run Perple_X, either point --config at this file and pass --perplex-dir on the command line, or merge these entries into a local configs/models.json that supplies perplex_dir.
_scope: Only literature-verified BSM entries. Not a runtime pipeline config. Not a place for surface proxies, hybrids, IBC derivations, unresolved models (moon_t82_highFe), Taylor, Sossi, O'Neill, Khan, PKT, KREEP, crust-extracted, cumulate, or arbitrary high-Fe compositions. See the study repository lunar-bsm-interior-models for the audit that produced this catalogue.
_reference_set_conclusion: TWO_REFERENCES_PLUS_SENSITIVITY: Hauri 2015 (primary), Warren 2005 Preferred BSM core-excluded (primary), Warren 2005 Alt Model 5 (within-framework sensitivity relative to Warren Preferred). The two Warren entries must NOT be treated as independent literature-level BSM estimates.
_common_implementation_basis: All entries reconstruct their oxides_wt_percent from a published source vector (source_oxides_wt_percent) via a documented transformation: retain the CFMAS+Ti oxide subset {SiO2, TiO2, Al2O3, FeO, MgO, CaO}, zero the remaining published oxides, and renormalize the retained subset to 100 wt%. Converting the published models to one common CFMAS+Ti basis is an IMPLEMENTATION TRANSFORMATION for the comparative study. It does NOT imply that the original publications used identical chemical systems or assumptions.
_common_thermodynamic_settings: All entries use database=hp633 (thermodynamic file hp633ver.dat, solution model file solution_model.dat, BUILD template lunar_hp633_template.build.in). The template gives pressure 1000 to 50000 bar (0.1 to 5 GPa), temperature 800 to 2200 K, an identical solid solution-model list (O(HP), Opx(HP), Cpx(HP), Gt(HP), Sp(HP), Pl(I1,HP), Ilm(WPH)), and identical silica-phase exclusions (q, crst, trd). No liquid model is active. Solid-only pilot; the rectangular P-T domain is not claimed to be thermodynamically valid everywhere.
_transformation_schema_version_note: Version of the source_transformation block schema attached to each model entry. Increment when the shape of source_transformation changes (adds/removes required keys). Downstream study snapshots (e.g., lunar-bsm-interior-models/configs/compositions/bsm_reference_set.json) refuse to sync if this version differs from the value they were built for.

models.description: Hauri (2015) BSM (Table 3, CFMAS+Ti reduction, core-excluded silicate inventory)
models.composition_interpretation: Hauri et al. (2015) BSM estimate derived from lunar volcanic-glass volatile and major-element data. Explicit BSM paper: Hauri 2015 Table 3 reports 'Estimated major and trace element composition of the bulk silicate Moon (BSM)'. Represents a global lunar silicate inventory after core formation; not automatically equivalent to a homogeneous present-day mantle.
models.source_note: Hauri, E. H., Saal, A. E., Rutherford, M. J., & Van Orman, J. A. (2015). Water in the Moon's interior: Truth and consequences. Earth and Planetary Science Letters, 409, 252-264. DOI: 10.1016/j.epsl.2014.10.053. Table 3 on printed page 257 (PDF page 6). Machine-readable transformation record is in the source_transformation block below.

source_transformation.publication: Hauri, Saal, Rutherford, Van Orman (2015), Earth and Planetary Science Letters 409, 252-264
source_transformation.row_label: Estimated major and trace element composition of the bulk silicate Moon (BSM)
source_transformation.normalization_basis: as reported; sum of listed oxides = 99.34 wt% (major elements only, before further transformation)
source_transformation.notes: FeO reported as FeO* (total iron as FeO) in Hauri Table 3. Retained-subset sum 99.05 = 45.00 + 0.20 + 4.45 + 8.05 + 37.80 + 3.55.

models.description: Warren (2005) Preferred BSM, core-excluded silicate inventory
models.composition_interpretation: Warren's central bulk-silicate-Moon (BSM) estimate, taken as the silicate inventory that remains after Warren's assumed 1.2 wt% core is excluded (Warren 2005 Table 6 row 'Same, excluding 1.2 wt% core'). Represents a global lunar silicate inventory after core formation; not automatically equivalent to a homogeneous present-day mantle. Related to moon_w05_alt5_feRich (Warren Alternative Model 5, MgO/FeO=3.4, Mg#=85.8, formerly moon_w05_moderateFe), which is the same Warren-family Fe-rich sensitivity endmember; the two configurations belong to the same paper and must NOT be presented as independent literature-level BSM estimates.
models.source_note: Warren, P. H. (2005). "New" lunar meteorites: Implications for composition of the global lunar surface, lunar crust, and the bulk Moon. Meteoritics & Planetary Science, 40(3), 477-506. DOI: 10.1111/j.1945-5100.2005.tb00395.x. Table 6 row 'Same, excluding 1.2 wt% core'. Machine-readable transformation record is in the source_transformation block below.

source_transformation.normalization_basis: core-excluded silicate; published row major-oxide sum ~99.15 + 0.132 (MnO) + 0.051 (Na2O) + 0.005 (K2O) + 0.44 (Cr2O3) plus trace Th = 100 (Warren's whole-Moon renormalization convention)
source_transformation.notes: Retained-subset sum 99.15 = 46.8 + 0.18 + 3.87 + 9.24 + 36.0 + 3.06. Full-precision renormalized (source x 1.008572869): SiO2 47.201210, TiO2 0.181543, Al2O3 3.903177, FeO 9.319213, MgO 36.308623, CaO 3.086233. Stored values are rounded to 2 decimals and sum to 100.00 wt%.

models._rename_note: Renamed from moon_w05_moderateFe on 2026-08-03 for scientific clarity: Mg#=85.8 is BELOW Warren Preferred's 87.4, so 'moderateFe' was directionally misleading. The new id 'alt5_feRich' matches Warren's own labelling of the row (Alt Model 5 under 'Alternative models, excluding core') and its scientific role (an Fe-rich sensitivity endmember). Composition, thermodynamic settings, and provenance are unchanged.
models.description: Warren (2005) Alternative Model 5 (within-framework Fe-rich sensitivity, core-excluded silicate)
models.composition_interpretation: Warren 2005 Alternative Model 5 (MgO/FeO = 3.4), a published Fe-rich silicate endmember listed under Warren Table 6's 'Alternative models, excluding core' header. This is a within-framework sensitivity relative to Warren's Preferred model (moon_w05_preferred_bsm), NOT an independent literature-level BSM estimate. The two Warren entries in this catalogue must not be presented as independent estimates of BSM uncertainty. Represents a global lunar silicate inventory after core formation; not automatically equivalent to a homogeneous present-day mantle.
models.source_note: Warren, P. H. (2005). "New" lunar meteorites: Implications for composition of the global lunar surface, lunar crust, and the bulk Moon. Meteoritics & Planetary Science, 40(3), 477-506. DOI: 10.1111/j.1945-5100.2005.tb00395.x. Table 6 row 'Alt 5, MgO/FeO = 3.4' (under 'Alternative models, excluding core' header). Machine-readable transformation record is in the source_transformation block below.

source_transformation.normalization_basis: core-excluded silicate; published row major-oxide sum ~99.15 plus minors 0.44+0.149+0.051+0.005 (Warren's whole-Moon renormalization convention)
